change: Move nine existing functional wrapper bodies unchanged from the shared header into libtorch_metadata.cc, isolating five torch/nn/functional headers. Public signatures remain unchanged.

adapter_comparison.method: Sequential compilations with copied include trees; before uses the base commit shared header, after uses the updated header. Same CPU SDK and compiler.
adapter_comparison.conclusion: Maximum RSS decreased by about 10%; wall time increased. These single-run samples demonstrate memory savings but do not establish a speedup.

measurement_limitations: GNU time maximum RSS is the maximum reported process RSS, not aggregate simultaneous memory. Existing Rust dependencies were retained. CPU/CUDA builds partly overlapped on a shared machine. These are not fresh Cargo target or controlled end-to-end before/after measurements; no end-to-end speedup is claimed.
coverage: Nine CPU functional parity tests cover all moved wrappers. CUDA helper run passes those nine tests with TERLAN_PYTORCH_REQUIRE_CUDA=1, plus ten CUDA tests. Generation produces 121 modules and 2829 functions; canonical source ownership matches.
remaining_cost: Header parsing and helper construction remain substantial; reuse or prebuild native helpers.
